items: Vertical measurement of the independence of a summit
books:
In topography, prominence (also referred to as autonomous height, and shoulder drop in US English, and drop in British English) is the height of the summit of a mountain or hill relative to the lowest contour line encircling it, but containing no higher summit within it. It is a measure of the independence of a summit. The key col ("saddle") around the peak is a unique point on this lowest contour line. The parent peak (if any) is some higher mountain, selected according to various criteria.
The prominence of a peak is the least drop in height necessary in order to get from the summit to any higher terrain.
